recall.minute: Traditional software fails from bugs in explicit logic; ML also fails from concept drift, corrupted and biased data, so tests cover data (schemas, missing values, distributions), models (performance, fairness, robustness), infrastructure (load, latency) and heuristics (age ≥ 0), arranged as a pyramid from data and code unit tests through model tests to system tests. The MLOps loop runs data validation, feature store, training, registry and CI/CD, deployment, monitoring and retraining. Data quality (accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness) is enforced with schema, value and label gates and an action gateway. Pipelines must be idempotent, versioned and orchestrated, with CI training on synthetic data for architecture changes. Model quality uses precision, recall, F1 and RMSE plus slicing, because 95% globally can hide a failing minority. Training tests check convergence and memory, inference tests check latency and shapes; telemetry covers system, model and business metrics. A/B, shadow and canary routing test in production. Threats include poisoning, backdoors, supply-chain attacks, evasion and model stealing. RAGAS evaluates RAG with faithfulness, answer relevance, context precision and context recall using an LLM judge.
